newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey EDA $2.75 bln pension bonds A-plus -S&P.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey EDA $2.75 bln pension bonds A-plus -S&P.

text.p: Standard & Poor's has assigned its A-plus rating to New Jersey Economic Development Authority's $2.75 billion state pension funding bonds.

The rating reflects the underlying creditworthiness of the state of New Jersey as obligor and the pledge of the state to pay debt service to the authority subject to annual legislative appropriation, S&P said. The agency also cited narrow legislative support for the issue offset partially by the state's long history of lease financing.
S&P issued the rating late on Friday.
The bonds are secured by a contract between the State Treasurer and the New Jersey Economic Development Authority.

The bond issue will fund the state's aggregate unfunded pension liability estimated to be $4.25 billion at March 31, 1996, comprised of $3.2 billion current liability and $1.05 billion future liability. The bonds will be amortized over a 35 year period, S&P said.
The pension bond proposal will create a fixed debt service obligation, however, S&P noted the state has been funding the unfunded pension liability on an annual basis.
